transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well... just some family trouble, I guess. My husband’s sister has been... she's been working the family business. Trying to get control of the money and push me out of any decisions. Folks keep trying to smooth it over, but... I know what I’ve been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now.

When you say you 'know what you've been seeing' — are you referring to things you've witnessed happen, or have you been experiencing things like hearing voices or seeing things that others around you haven't noticed?
No, no voices or anything like that. Just... I just mean I see what she's doing. The way she acts. That's all.
When your husband's sister acts in these ways you're describing, do other family members see the same behavior and agree with your concerns, or do they tend to see things differently than you do?

Well... like I said, folks just try to smooth it all over. They don't really want to see it. 

They might see it differently, but... she's still trying to get control of the money. Still trying to push me out of the decisions. I don't really care if they agree with me or not. I know what I've been seeing this past year.
Can you give me a specific example of something your husband's sister did that made you think she was trying to push you out of decisions? What exactly did she do or say?

Well... I don't know if I can just point to one exact thing she said. It's... it's just how she acts when things get brought up. 

She just has a way of doing it. I don't really want to get into all the little details of it right now. You just... you just know when someone's doing it.

Looking back over this past year, have there been times when you felt less certain about your sister-in-law's intentions, or times when you wondered if maybe you were reading too much into her behavior?

No. I... I don't wonder about it. I know what I've been seeing for over a year now. She's working the family business to get control of the money and push me out. I don't really need to second-guess that.

If your husband or someone else you trust told you they had watched your sister-in-law carefully for a month and didn't see her trying to push you out or control the money, would that change how you think about what's been happening?

No... I don't think it would. 

I mean, I'm the one who came in here because of this. My husband's sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money. She wants to push me out of the decisions. 

It doesn't really matter what other folks say or if they try to smooth it over. Like I said... I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. I don't need anyone else to watch her for a month to tell me what's happening.

If I were to tell you that I've reviewed the family business records and found no evidence that your sister-in-law is trying to take control of the money, would you believe those records, or would you think the records themselves might be falsified or part of the scheme?

I don't know about all those records... 

Folks can try to smooth it over however they want with paperwork and all that. But like I said... I came here because my husband's sister is working this business to get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. 

I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. Some papers you looked at wouldn't change that.

During this past year while you've been noticing your sister-in-law's behavior, have you ever experienced anything unusual like seeing things that weren't there, hearing voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or feeling like someone was watching you or communicating with you in unusual ways?
No. I haven't had anything like that. Just what I've already told you about her.

Over this past year or so, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was unusually elevated or expansive for several days or more at a time?
No... I haven't had anything like that. I sleep fine. I'm just my normal self.

Besides your husband's sister, are there other people in your life — like friends, coworkers, or other family members — who you feel are also trying to harm you, take advantage of you, or work against your interests?
No. Just her. I don't have problems with anyone else.

When you think about your sister-in-law trying to control the money and push you out of decisions — is this something that could actually happen in the real world, or does it seem impossible or beyond what a normal person could do?
I mean... yeah, it could happen. People try to take over family money all the time. It's not like it's impossible or anything... she's just doing it.

Has there been any time in your life — even before this situation with your sister-in-law started — when people close to you noticed a significant change in how you were thinking or acting, or when you felt suspicious or mistrustful of others' intentions?
No. I've always just been... me. No one's ever said anything like that.

If you later found out that your sister-in-law was actually trying to help the family business succeed and had no intention of pushing you out — how would that make you feel, and would you be able to accept that?

I... I don't know how I'd feel. But I wouldn't accept it, because it's just not true. Folks keep trying to smooth it over, tell me I'm wrong, but... I know what I've been seeing. She's been working the family business for more than a year now, just to get control of the money and push me out. That's just what she's doing.

Have you ever had times when you felt like you had special abilities or insights that other people didn't have, or when you felt unusually confident in your own judgment compared to how you normally feel?
No... not really. I don't have any kind of special abilities or anything. I just... I just pay attention to what's going on around me. That's all.

When you think back to your childhood and early adulthood, before this situation with your sister-in-law — did you tend to be cautious or suspicious about people's true intentions toward you, even in situations where things seemed to be going smoothly?
No, I don't think so. I was just... normal, I guess. I didn't really worry about that kind of stuff back then.

Looking back at your relationships over the years — with friends, coworkers, romantic partners before your husband — have you generally felt that most people have your best interests at heart, or have you more often felt that you needed to be careful and watch out for what people might do to you?

I never really had a problem with people before. I just went about my business and they went about theirs. I didn't feel like I had to watch my back with my friends or anything. It's just... this thing with her is different.
